q-12244.name: Question 1
q-12244.worked_solution:
Writing the radical as a rational exponent, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}=\frac{1}{{x}^{1/2}}={x}^{-1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the power rule with $n=-\frac{1}{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-1/2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2\,-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-3/2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{3/2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-12244.html:
Question 1
?

Find dydx when y=1x.

a
−x2
b
−2x3
c
x2
d
−12x3
e
1x3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Writing the radical as a rational exponent, we have y=1x=1x1/2=x−1/2. Applying the power rule with n=−12, we get dydx=ddx(x−1/2)=−12x−1/2−1=−12x−3/2=−12x3/2=−12x3.
